what: Nato leaders meet in Turkey for summit after Trump renews calls for US to take over Greenland – Europe live

clean_source_blocks.text: Meeting begins this morning after president threatens to pull American troops out of Europe as he arrived in Ankara yesterday Trump renews call for US to take over Greenland as he arrives for Nato summit Nato leaders are meeting in Ankara, Turkey today for what was meant to be a “Trump-proof” summit: short and sweet, with little space for any drama or outbursts from the notoriously unpredictable US president. Yeah, good luck with that. Continue reading...

Let’s see how it all unfolds with grumpy Trump in the audience though. Nato leaders are meeting in Ankara, Turkey today for what was meant to be a “Trump-proof” summit: short and sweet, with little space for any drama or outbursts from the notoriously unpredictable US president. Even before the summit proper began, Trump lashed out against several Nato allies saying he was “very disappointed” that “they were not there” for the US on Iran, threatened to pull out US troops from Europe, and repeated his claim that Greenland should be controlled by the US, not Denmark. Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen was forced to say this morning that her country was “ready to defend” Greenland if needed, reiterating the territory was “not for sale.”

WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump reignited his call for the United States to control Greenland, threatening to remove American soldiers from European nations over the issue, as the 2026 NATO summit got underway in Ankara on July 7. Trump reiterated his position that Greenland is vital for U.S. security during a bilateral meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan after an earlier push from Trump to acquire the semi-autonomous territory from Denmark set off a NATO crisis in January. "That's what hurt my relationship with NATO," Trump said in response to a reporter's question about Greenland. "Because Greenland doesn't help Denmark. Denmark doesn't spend money to really help Greenland, but it's an important part for the United States, and it's surrounded by China ships and Russian ships, and that's not going to happen."

Referring to Greenland, Trump added: "That should be controlled by the United States, not by Denmark." More: Trump calls off tariffs after touting 'framework' for Greenland deal Trump took NATO to the brink of disaster in January before he eventually ruled out military action to acquire Greenland and pulled back threats to impose tariffs on European allies. Tensions deescalated after Trump announced the "framework of a future deal" with NATO, Denmark and the Arctic region on security matters. Trump's Greenland talks died down over the following months, yet Trump introduced a new threat at the NATO summit in Turkey: removing U.S. soldiers from Europe over the continent's opposition.

Arriving early for the summit, Nato’s Rutte said the meeting was “about implementation, about getting it done” after last year’s push to increase defence spending.

He said that European allies and Canada were “stepping up” with more money, more jobs, and more capacity, but there is still more to be done.

“If you look at it from the United States perspective, you will have European allies which are much more capable, with the US, to work together in Nato to keep one billion people safe,” he said, repeatedly praising Trump for pushing Europe to do more.

Rutte also said the meeting was about reiterating the alliance’s support for Ukraine, expecting the leaders to agree on “a strong commitment to keep supporting Ukraine.”

He said he expected the leaders to “acknowledge collectively that Russia is the long-term threat” to Nato.

Let’s see how it all unfolds with grumpy Trump in the audience though.

Nato leaders are meeting in Ankara, Turkey today for what was meant to be a “Trump-proof” summit: short and sweet, with little space for any drama or outbursts from the notoriously unpredictable US president.

Even before the summit proper began, Trump lashed out against several Nato allies saying he was “very disappointed” that “they were not there” for the US on Iran, threatened to pull out US troops from Europe, and repeated his claim that Greenland should be controlled by the US, not Denmark.

Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen was forced to say this morning that her country was “ready to defend” Greenland if needed, reiterating the territory was “not for sale.”

Expect more of the same today, as Trump is due to show up shortly, accompanied by secretary general Mark Rutte, who has the impossible job of keeping him on side.

The formal welcome ceremony gets under way shortly at 10:45am Turkish time (that’s 8:45am UK time, and 9:45am CEST), where we will get all sorts of official photos.

The proper session starts at 11.15 (9:15am UK), and will last only for a few hours. We are then going to hear from leaders about how well (or not) it went.

It’s Wednesday, 8 July 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

payload.title: Trumpin Grönlanti-puhe varjostaa Naton huippukokousta Ankarassa
payload.summary: Naton johtajat kokoontuvat Turkissa huippukokoukseen, jota hallitsevat Donald Trumpin uudet vaatimukset Grönlannin hallinnasta ja uhkaus vetää yhdysvaltalaissotilaita pois Euroopasta.
payload.content:
Naton johtajat kokoontuvat Ankarassa huippukokoukseen tilanteessa, jossa Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on jälleen vaatinut Grönlannin siirtämistä Yhdysvaltain hallintaan ja uhannut poistaa amerikkalaisia sotilaita Euroopasta. Kokouksesta oli tarkoitus tehdä lyhyt ja hallittu, jotta liittokunnan sisäisille yhteenotoille jäisi mahdollisimman vähän tilaa, mutta Trumpin lausunnot nostivat Grönlannin heti kokouksen keskeiseksi kiistaksi.

## Grönlanti nousi uudelleen esiin

Trump toisti kantansa saavuttuaan Turkkiin Naton vuoden 2026 huippukokoukseen. Hänen mukaansa Grönlanti on tärkeä Yhdysvaltain turvallisuudelle, eikä alueen pitäisi olla Tanskan vaan Yhdysvaltain hallinnassa. Hän puhui asiasta myös kahdenvälisessä tapaamisessa Turkin presidentin Recep Tayyip Erdoğanin kanssa.

Toimittajan kysymykseen vastatessaan Trump sanoi, että Grönlanti oli vahingoittanut hänen suhdettaan Natoon. Hän perusteli vaatimustaan sillä, ettei Tanska hänen mukaansa käytä riittävästi rahaa Grönlannin auttamiseen. Trump viittasi lisäksi Kiinan ja Venäjän aluksiin alueen ympäristössä ja sanoi, ettei tilanne voi jatkua sellaisena.

Tanskan pääministeri Mette Frederiksen vastasi aamulla, että Tanska on valmis puolustamaan Grönlantia tarvittaessa. Hän myös toisti, ettei Grönlanti ole myytävänä.

## Joukkojen vetäminen kiristää painetta

Trumpin ulostulo tuli ennen varsinaisen huippukokouksen alkua. Hän arvosteli useita Nato-liittolaisia ja sanoi olevansa hyvin pettynyt siihen, etteivät ne hänen mukaansa olleet Yhdysvaltojen tukena Irania koskevassa tilanteessa. Samalla hän uhkasi vetää yhdysvaltalaisia joukkoja pois Euroopasta. Uhkaus liittyi lähteiden mukaan Euroopan vastustukseen Grönlantia koskevassa kysymyksessä.

Grönlanti aiheutti Nato-kriisin jo tammikuussa, kun Trumpin aiempi pyrkimys hankkia Tanskalle kuuluva itsehallintoalue kiristi suhteita liittolaisiin. Tuolloin hän lopulta sulki pois sotilaallisen toiminnan Grönlannin hankkimiseksi ja perääntyi myös uhkauksista asettaa tulleja eurooppalaisille liittolaisille.

Jännitteet hellittivät myöhemmin, kun Trump ilmoitti tulevan sopimuksen kehyksestä Naton, Tanskan ja arktisen alueen turvallisuuskysymyksissä. Ankaran kokouksen alku osoittaa kuitenkin, että Grönlanti ei ole kadonnut liittokunnan sisäisten kiistojen listalta.
summary_bullets: Naton johtajat kokoontuvat Ankarassa huippukokoukseen Trumpin Grönlanti-lausuntojen varjossa.
Trump vaatii jälleen, että Grönlannin tulisi olla Yhdysvaltain eikä Tanskan hallinnassa.
Tanskan Mette Frederiksen sanoo, että Grönlanti ei ole myytävänä ja että Tanska on valmis puolustamaan aluetta.
Trump on uhannut vetää yhdysvaltalaisia sotilaita pois Euroopasta.

Let’s see how it all unfolds with grumpy Trump in the audience though. Nato leaders are meeting in Ankara, Turkey today for what was meant to be a “Trump-proof” summit: short and sweet, with little space for any drama or outbursts from the notoriously unpredictable US president. Even before the summit proper began, Trump lashed out against several Nato allies saying he was “very disappointed” that “they were not there” for the US on Iran, threatened to pull out US troops from Europe, and repeated his claim that Greenland should be controlled by the US, not Denmark. Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen was forced to say this morning that her country was “ready to defend” Greenland if needed, reiterating the territory was “not for sale.”

WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump reignited his call for the United States to control Greenland, threatening to remove American soldiers from European nations over the issue, as the 2026 NATO summit got underway in Ankara on July 7. Trump reiterated his position that Greenland is vital for U.S. security during a bilateral meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan after an earlier push from Trump to acquire the semi-autonomous territory from Denmark set off a NATO crisis in January. "That's what hurt my relationship with NATO," Trump said in response to a reporter's question about Greenland. "Because Greenland doesn't help Denmark. Denmark doesn't spend money to really help Greenland, but it's an important part for the United States, and it's surrounded by China ships and Russian ships, and that's not going to happen."

Referring to Greenland, Trump added: "That should be controlled by the United States, not by Denmark." More: Trump calls off tariffs after touting 'framework' for Greenland deal Trump took NATO to the brink of disaster in January before he eventually ruled out military action to acquire Greenland and pulled back threats to impose tariffs on European allies. Tensions deescalated after Trump announced the "framework of a future deal" with NATO, Denmark and the Arctic region on security matters. Trump's Greenland talks died down over the following months, yet Trump introduced a new threat at the NATO summit in Turkey: removing U.S. soldiers from Europe over the continent's opposition.
